findings.claim: When the reviewer does not answer on the re-ask, Launch returns the second call's error instead of the first refusal, although S7 says "a reviewer that does not answer" returns "the first error as today"; so a codex/claude failure on the re-ask turns the outcome of `review launch` from exit 2 (refusal of the reply it did get) into exit 1 (codex failure), a behavior change the re-ask was meant not to make.
evidence: launch.go:86-88: `if reply, err = s.reviewer.Review(bound.Worktree, model, again); err != nil { return Recorded{}, err }` overwrites err with the reviewer error; the first *ReplyRefusedError held in the earlier `err` (line 81) is discarded.

odd/tasks/phase9-c25-review-hunt.md:14 (S7): "any other refusal, a reviewer that does not answer, and a re-ask over `review.MaxReplyBytes` return the first error as today" - the re-ask-over-bound case is listed alongside it, so the list describes outcomes during the re-ask.
app.go:254-262 / usage text: *ReplyRefusedError maps to exit 2, any other failure to exit 1; the Reviewer port wraps ErrReviewerDidNotAnswer, which is not a ReplyRefusedError (launch.go:13-22).
launch_test.go in the diff has no test where the second Review call fails (fakeReviewer.err applies to every call; no test sets it with replies), so this path is unpinned either way.
